walkthroughs.body_html:
Area of Study 1: Instrumental Music of Haydn, Mozart and Beethoven — a core area of A-Level Music.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Area of Study 1: Instrumental Music of Haydn, Mozart and Beethoven brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Area of Study 1: Instrumental Music of Haydn, Mozart and Beethoven.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What distinguishes Classical (1750-1820) from Baroque style?
options: Clearer melodic phrases, homophonic texture, balanced structures like sonata form.
Classical means any old serious music.
Any three notes played together.
Use of orchestra (Baroque had none).

mcqs.q: What three notes form a major triad in root position?
options: Classical means any old serious music.
Any three notes played together.
Three consecutive scale notes.
Root, major third, perfect fifth.

mcqs.q: Which chords form a plagal cadence?
options: Any three notes played together.
V to I.
ii to V.
IV to I (the 'amen' cadence).
